description: §4.12.4 — the OVER-FIRE GUARD for the S356 execution-context gate. A nested `<program name="doubler">` carrying nothing but `name=` IS the inline web worker: it is extracted, it gets a `new Worker(...)` reference and a real worker bundle, and it compiles clean. Neither E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL nor W-PROGRAM-TOP-LEVEL-NAME may fire on it. Without this case the gate could be satisfied by refusing every nested `<program>`, which would break the one execution context that works.
rationale: §4.12.3: "Inline web worker | `name=`, no `lang=` | `new Worker()`, postMessage IPC". §4.12.4: "A nested `<program>` with no `lang=` attribute is an inline web worker declaration. The compiler generates a `Worker` instantiation and postMessage-based IPC." §4.12.8 gives the communication model this case exercises in both directions — `<#name>.send(value)` parent-to-child, `send(value)` inside the `when message` handler child-to-parent.
